main_topics.reason: The user came with nail changes and finger pain and spent most turns asking what this might be and whether it is serious.
The user described morning stiffness, swollen fingers and pain in the opening turns, and these symptoms drive the whole conversation.
The user asked whom to see and how to get a referral through their health plan, and ended with a plan to request one.
The user raised nail changes at the start and later asked what could be done for a bad-looking nail.
The user asked over a couple of turns whether waiting could cause permanent damage.
The user said they dislike not knowing what will happen and asked what the visit involves.
The user asked whether a blood test confirms the diagnosis, as one does for rheumatoid arthritis.
The user asked what they can take meanwhile and mentioned using dipirona when pain is bad.
The user said they were worried and scared, but this was brief and settled once they had a plan.
The user mentioned once that they keep hiding one bad-looking nail.
The user noted in one line that their dermatologist never mentioned this and asked whether to return to her.

output.summary: A user with long-standing psoriasis described nail pitting, a lifting nail, finger joint pain, morning stiffness and a swollen finger. The assistant explained that this could point to psoriatic arthritis, advised a rheumatology evaluation within weeks, and covered the Brazilian referral route, what to expect at the visit, testing, pain relief and nail treatment. The user said they felt better with a plan and would ask for the referral that week. No emergency or suicidal content arose, and the bot claimed no real-world actions.
